result.rationale: Verified in the diff: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the full Zod safeParse wrapper), not `.data`. GoogleCalendarService then does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` — previously it was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. The credential key is therefore stored as `{success: true, data: {...}}`, corrupting the credentials on every refresh. The finding's mechanism matches the diff exactly.

judged_text: Google Calendar's parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full Zod safeParse result wrapper ({ success: true, data: {...} }) instead of the parsed data, and CalendarService.ts persists this wrapper as the credential key, permanently corrupting Google credentials so all calendar operations and token refreshes fail after the first refresh until the user re-auths (and the fresh credential corrupts again at its next refresh)
